claim: Knowledge about the natural world comes primarily from sensory experience and observation

evidence.title: Empiricism (SEP)
evidence.finding: Empiricism holds that knowledge comes from sensory experience; foundational to modern science since Bacon and Locke

evidence.title: Theory and Observation in Science (SEP)
evidence.finding: While observations are theory-laden, empirical evidence remains the primary arbiter of scientific claims

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Empiricism itself is a philosophical position, not directly measurable; but empirical methods demonstrably produce knowledge
scoreReasoning.coherence: Foundational to the entire scientific worldview and consistent with naturalism
scoreReasoning.convergence: Broadly accepted in science; philosophers debate the extent to which observation is theory-independent
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: All experimental science is built on empiricist methodology

claim: A hypothesis must be potentially falsifiable by observation to be scientifically meaningful

evidence.title: Karl Popper (SEP)
evidence.finding: Popper proposed falsifiability as the criterion demarcating science from non-science; influential but debated

evidence.title: Science and Pseudo-Science (SEP)
evidence.finding: Falsifiability remains the most influential demarcation criterion despite known limitations (Duhem-Quine problem)

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Falsifiability is a philosophical criterion, not itself empirically testable
scoreReasoning.coherence: Generally consistent with scientific practice but has known edge cases (string theory, multiverse)
scoreReasoning.convergence: Widely cited as a demarcation criterion; significant philosophical criticism from Kuhn, Lakatos, Feyerabend
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Practically useful for distinguishing testable from untestable claims in science

claim: Controlled experiments isolating variables can establish causal relationships

evidence.title: Counterfactual Theories of Causation (SEP)
evidence.finding: Controlled experiments operationalize counterfactual reasoning to establish causal relationships

evidence.title: Randomised controlled trials (BMJ)
evidence.finding: RCTs are considered the gold standard for establishing causal claims in medicine and social science

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Controlled experiments directly measure causal relationships by manipulating variables; strong empirical track record
scoreReasoning.coherence: Central methodology of modern science, consistent with causal reasoning frameworks
scoreReasoning.convergence: Broad agreement on the power of controlled experiments; debates about external validity and generalizability
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Pharmaceutical development, engineering, agriculture all depend on controlled experimentation

claim: Independent replication and peer critique improve the reliability of scientific claims

evidence.title: Estimating the reproducibility of psychological science (Open Science Collaboration)
evidence.finding: Large-scale replication effort found only 36-47% of psychology studies replicated, highlighting both the value and limitations of peer review

evidence.title: Scientific Objectivity (SEP)
evidence.finding: Peer review and replication are key mechanisms for achieving intersubjective agreement in science

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Replication studies provide direct evidence; the replication crisis reveals both the method's importance and current failures
scoreReasoning.coherence: Core component of scientific methodology; consistent with fallibilist epistemology
scoreReasoning.convergence: Agreement that peer review helps, but significant concern about its effectiveness given the replication crisis
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Peer review catches errors and fraud, though imperfectly; no better alternative exists at scale

claim: Rational belief revision follows probabilistic updating on new evidence

evidence.title: Bayesian Epistemology (SEP)
evidence.finding: Bayesian epistemology provides a formal framework for updating beliefs in light of evidence using Bayes' theorem

evidence.title: Philosophy of Statistics (SEP)
evidence.finding: Bayesian methods are increasingly used in science alongside frequentist approaches for inference and decision-making

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Bayesianism is a normative framework — it prescribes how reasoning should work, not a directly measurable phenomenon
scoreReasoning.coherence: Mathematically rigorous, consistent with probability theory and decision theory
scoreReasoning.convergence: Growing acceptance in philosophy and science; ongoing debate with frequentist approaches
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Bayesian methods are practically powerful in machine learning, medicine, and scientific inference

claim: Convergence of independent researchers using diverse methods strengthens evidential support for claims

evidence.title: Underdetermination of Scientific Theory (SEP)
evidence.finding: Consilience of evidence from multiple independent lines of investigation is a key mark of well-supported theories

evidence.title: Expert credibility in climate change (Anderegg et al.)
evidence.finding: 97% of actively publishing climate scientists agree on anthropogenic climate change, demonstrating how consensus forms around strong evidence

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Consensus formation can be observed and measured (surveys, citation analysis) but its reliability as a knowledge indicator is debated
scoreReasoning.coherence: Consistent with the principle that independent convergence is unlikely to be coincidental
scoreReasoning.convergence: Broad agreement that consensus matters; debate about when consensus reflects truth vs groupthink
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Scientific consensus guides policy, technology development, and medical practice effectively

claim: The scientific method, combining empiricism with systematic hypothesis testing, is the most reliable method for generating knowledge about the natural world

evidence.title: Scientific Method (SEP)
evidence.finding: The scientific method combines observation, hypothesis formation, testing, and revision in a self-correcting cycle

evidence.title: Scientific Progress (SEP)
evidence.finding: Science has demonstrably progressed in predictive and explanatory power over centuries, though the mechanism of progress is debated

scoreReasoning.correspondence: The claim that science is 'most reliable' is comparative and not directly measurable by a single experiment
scoreReasoning.coherence: Deeply coherent with the history and philosophy of science; well-supported by the track record argument
scoreReasoning.convergence: Broadly accepted by scientists and most philosophers; postmodernist and sociological critiques exist but are minority positions
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: The technological and medical revolutions provide overwhelming pragmatic evidence for the effectiveness of scientific method
